steps.content: The last of the flames sputters and dies, and with them, the sounds of Marlo's massacre fall silent.

In the hazy, smoke-choked aftermath, you follow Hilda through the dim corridors, the acrid stench of burning saturating the air. She leads you to the hall that has been utterly transformed into a scene of chaos.
Here, the survivors have gathered.
Nolaine crouches by the doorway, a gun hanging limply in her hand. She stares with profound shock at the dozens of corpses littering the floor.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: ...******* hell. That was brutal.
Before the sprawl of corpses, Marlo sits on the sofa, a god of slaughter soaked in blood.

steps.speaker: Marlo
steps.content: Report, ma'am. All 29 security guards who were disguised traitors have been eliminated.

steps.speaker: Marlo
steps.content: That old dog Huck tried to slip away in the chaos. I put him down with one shot, too.

steps.speaker: Marlo
steps.content: Not sure if the actual mole was among them, but if you interrogate that survivor, you'll get something useful.
His hand trembles as he fumbles for a cigarette. But his strength is gone; his fingers betray him, and it tumbles from his grasp, unlit.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: You idiot! Are you trying to get yourself killed?!
With reddened eyes, Helene sits down beside him and lights the cigarette for him.

steps.speaker: Marlo
steps.content: Heh... after all this time... never learned to do anything but kill. Guess you could call it playing to my strengths.

steps.speaker: Marlo
steps.content: I've spent half my life killing. My hands are stained, my soul is stained. Can't wash it clean. When I die, hell's the only place that'll have me...

steps.speaker: Marlo
steps.content: Hilda, I... I've always been on the level. The ones I didn't kill, I didn't. The ones I did, I own up to every one.

steps.speaker: Marlo
steps.content: Remember this... I'm not the mole... I... never betrayed the city-state...

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...I know. Why else would I have untied you?

steps.speaker: Marlo
steps.content: Heh... Heh, good... Looks like... this was part of your plan too... that's good... that's good...

steps.speaker: Marlo
steps.content: Among us... as long as you stay on the right path... everything's fine...
(Black Screen)
His voice grows faint, dies away, and in the void it leaves behind, a new one arises: the soft, unmistakable sound of someone reciting poetry.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: ...Ah, fate...
Ah, fate! You blind thrower of dice, casting us onto fields shrouded in war. Young hearts, once flowing freely like spring waters, now bewildered, trembling beneath iron hooves.
The future is a wasteland veiled in mist, a deafened horn, a silent summon. To voyage without a map, how treacherous. The destination, perhaps just an unsealed coffin...
(End of Black Screen)
Hilda gently closes his eyes.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...Rest in peace now, Marlo. The city-state will not forget you.
